title: Twinleaf Logistics - Governance & Ops Onboarding Ignition
summary: Kickoff focused on Twinleaf's security and network requirements for Redwood Private, initial staging plan, success criteria for pilot (latency < 150ms median, P95 < 400ms, data residency in eu-west-1), and next-step deliverables (security pack, pilot SOW, staging credentials). SE to run simple latency benchmark and share runbook.
next_steps: Alex to send tailored security packet and SOW draft by 2026-08-24
Jordan to run initial latency benchmark using Twinleaf sample prompts and share results by 2026-08-26
Liam to provide VPC peering contact and network diagrams by 2026-08-25
Priya to schedule pilot kickoff and internal enablement on 2026-09-01
action_items: Jordan Miles - Run baseline latency/cost benchmark against hosted vs dedicated profile - due 2026-08-26
Alex Chen - Share Redwood Private security checklist, SOC2 docs, and SAML SSO integration notes - due 2026-08-24
Liam O'Neill - Export network topology and firewall rules for staging VPC - due 2026-08-25

transcript:
Meeting Header:
Date: 2026-08-21 15:00 UTC
Duration: 46 minutes
Attendees: Alex (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood CSM), Jordan (Redwood SE), Marta (Twinleaf CTO), Liam (Twinleaf Infra), Sasha (Data Platform), Ren (PM)

[00:00] Alex: hey everyone thanks for joining the kickoff for the Twinleaf pilot, i know it's a busy week so we'll try to be sharp and action oriented. i'm alex, i'll lead the engagement from an account side. priya will run ops and onboarding. jordan and diego from eng are on for technical bits.
[00:18] Marta: yeah thanks, we'll try to keep it tight. our main ask is we need to validate private deployment in eu-west-1, data residency and audit trail is a must. also low tail latency for our customer-facing summaries.
[00:32] Priya: great, noted. high-level agenda: security and compliance, network/topology, pilot success metrics, timeline and owners. any other items to add?
[00:40] Liam: just network specifics — we need to confirm peering options and if Redwood requires private link or direct connect style setup.
[00:47] Jordan: quick note: for the pilot we can do either Redwood Hosted with VPC peering or Redwood Private (customer-managed control plane). there are tradeoffs on latency and operational ownership.
[01:05] Marta: so if we can get sub 150ms median for the core summarize flow, that's acceptable, P95 ideally under 400ms. cost also matters but latency first.
[01:18] Alex: understood, we'll treat those as pilot SLAs. do you have typical request QPS and payload sizes?
[01:25] Sasha: on production we'd be ~20 qps sustained on peak, but pilot will be small, maybe 2-3 qps with representative docs. payloads are 1-3k tokens typically per request.
[01:36] Jordan: ok that helps. rough note: hosted will get you faster onboarding, dedicated/dedicated private instances lower variance at scale. but we can run a quick bench for both.

[02:05] (15s cross-talk)
[02:20] Ren: timeline question — how long to stand up staging private deployment?
[02:26] Alex: typical is 2-3 weeks for Private staging if network and creds are ready; hosted pilot can start in days. we'll try to overlap security review and infra prep.
[02:39] Marta: we do have a compliance review next month so we'd prefer the control plane to be our VPC if possible. also KMS integration is required for keys.
[02:50] Priya: confirms, Redwood Private supports customer-managed KMS/HSM — we'll include the KMS integration notes in the security packet.
[03:04] Liam: firewall rules — do you need inbound or outbound open ranges? we run pretty strict egress rules.
[03:12] Jordan: primarily outbound to Redwood control plane for telemetry; for private we can arrange peering and keep control-plane comms in the peered network. we'll share exact CIDR and port lists.
[03:25] Alex: action: liam, please share your network diagram and existing peering account contact; jordan will map the required ports and create a network workbook.

[03:45] Sasha: question on data retention — we need logs for audit but have to redact PII. can Redwood redact or do we need a pre-processing step?
[03:57] Diego: from support: Redwood can redact at ingestion for common PII patterns, and audit logs are configurable. for extra protection we recommend a small pre-processing lambda on customer side for deterministic redaction.
[04:16] Marta: okay we'll scope redaction in the SOW.

[04:30] (minute marker)
[05:00] Jordan: going into runbook specifics — we'll start with a minimal model profile: our curated 7B open model variant in quantized int8, sequence length up to 4k, and enable KV cache. we'll measure cold start and steady state latency.
[05:20] Marta: will that be compatible with our summarization prompt? we have few-shot templates and tool-calling.
[05:27] Jordan: yes we can support tool calling patterns; if you need function-calling we'll map the schema. there may be some tokenizer differences but we'll handle that in validation.
[05:39] Sasha: note — our team currently uses in-house embeddings for search, but we're considering switching to Redwood embeddings for cost. any migration caveats?
[05:50] Alex: migration notes: we can run A/B against existing embeddings and provide cost delta analysis; depending on vector dimension and storage you'll likely see cost decreases via Redwood's batching and caching recommendations.

[06:15] Ren: what's the uptimes and SLA for Private?
[06:20] Priya: Private is typically offered with an enterprise SLA for uptime; dedicated capacity options get tighter latency SLOs. we'll include exact SLA and escalation matrix in the packet.

[06:40] (brief pause)
[07:05] Marta: security stack — we need SOC2 attestation, ISO 27001 if available, SAML SSO, audit logs retention options to 7 years. is that in scope?
[07:16] Alex: SOC2 yes, ISO depending on timeline; SAML and audit logs are supported. long term retention we can discuss as an add-on. we'll surface current certifications.
[07:29] Liam: also need to know about data residency for backups and logs — must stay eu-west-1.
[07:36] Diego: backup and logs location adjustable for Private; we'll document exact storage endpoints.

[08:00] Jordan: architecture note: for low-latency we recommend colocating inference nodes in same region as API gateway and enabling prefix caching for repeated prompts; that reduces token cost and latency.
[08:14] Marta: prefix / KV caching — explain that briefly, we heard of kv cache but not sure of integration steps.
[08:20] Jordan: kv cache stores prior attention key/values for the conversation; for repeated summarization it avoids recomputing previous tokens. it's simple to enable in the runbook and needs a small amount of shared memory on the inference nodes.

[09:05] Sasha: question — are there any managed webhooks for function call results? we need guaranteed delivery.
[09:12] Jordan: yes we provide webhook retries and dead-lettering for failed calls; for mission-critical flows we recommend idempotent handling and acks.

[09:40] Ren: ok curious about cost — what's the expected ballpark for the pilot per 1k tokens?
[09:45] Alex: rough numbers depend a lot on model size/quantization and batching; we'll share a cost estimate example. for the pilot we can do a fixed tranche to limit exposure.

[10:10] (15s side chatter)
[10:30] Priya: timeline propose: this week network export; next week security packet and SOW; following week staging deploy and initial bench. target pilot kickoff 2026-09-01 as discussed.
[10:45] Marta: that works for us.

[11:00] Jordan: technical checkpoint — i want a sample of your few-shot templates and representative documents. something anonymized. that'll make the benchmark meaningful.
[11:10] Sasha: we'll produce a sanitized dataset and schema by Friday.

[11:30] Alex: i'll send an intro email with links: security packet, SOW template, runbook skeleton, and a shared benchmark sheet.

[11:45] Marta: any blockers we foresee? internal procurement needs 2 weeks once SOW is approved. also our infra team needs to schedule maintenance windows for peering.
[11:58] Priya: we'll factor procurement into timeline and provide a sample procurement clause to speed legal review.

[12:15] Ren: shall we schedule a quick 30m pre-kickoff next week for the infra folks?
[12:22] Alex: yes priya will send a calendar invite; prefer next tuesday morning.

[12:35] (wrap)
[12:40] Alex: recap: Jordan runs bench, Alex and Priya share docs, Liam exports network, Sasha shares sanitized prompts, Priya books pilot kickoff. we'll aim to meet the dates in the action items. thanks everyone.
[12:50] Marta: thanks all, look forward to it.

End of transcript.
